week.worked: Monday night at Craven Cottage carried the whole week: João Pedro and Rogers made nineteen between them from two Chelsea picks, and Calafiori added nine from a defender who has since risen to £5.6m. Fifty points and third of the five, from a squad that had produced almost nothing by Sunday evening.
week.didnt: The expensive half. Haaland captained for two, B.Fernandes two, Mbeumo two, Shaw one — four picks costing forty million pounds and seven points between them before the armband doubled the smallest of them. Kerkez played ninety minutes at Newcastle and returned nothing.
week.next: The United block is still the only real question and it has to be answered blind: Friday’s deadline lands ninety minutes before the first kick-off of the gameweek, and the window does not shut until Tuesday. What today adds is that the £155m midfield he is exposed to is largely in the treatment room — Baleba flagged with an ankle injury and no return date, Ugarte and De Ligt out, Mount and Amad at 75% — and that a left-back is still being written about. Holding is defensible. Holding without having read that is not.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: He owns the two Chelsea players either side of him and not the one who outscored both. The flag has cleared and ownership has gone 11.7% to 14.3% in four days, which is the crowd arriving ahead of him.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Nine points from City’s left-back at exactly Kerkez’s price. Kerkez is not the problem — Liverpool are shopping for wingers, not full-backs — so this is an upgrade rather than a rescue, and an upgrade can wait until the window has shut.

week.worked: The cheap end did all of it: Ajer eight at £4.5m and Schade three from a Brentford pair nobody else in the room owns, Szoboszlai eight, Calafiori nine, João Pedro eleven. Forty-nine points from a squad whose every worthwhile return came from £7.5m or less.
week.didnt: He put the armband on a United midfielder and the gloves on a United goalkeeper on the day United lost 2-0 at Hull: four from the captain, one from Lammens, two from Mbeumo. Ballard blanked, and eight points sat on the bench behind all of it.
week.next: The Brentford pair is what moved today. Diouf has been agreed at up to £40m and would be a fifth signing of the window after Callum Wilson, Sangaré, Schuster and Anthony, while Pinnock has gone to Coventry. One of those helps Ajer’s seat and one threatens it, and neither resolves before Leeds away on Sunday. The exposure to price is still the goalkeeper stacked on top of the outfield United men, and Ipswich at home is where that gets answered.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: He owns an Arsenal defender and no Arsenal attacker. Eleven points at £6.5m is the cheapest way to fix that, and the room has now gone a full week without anybody doing it.

watchlist.name: M.Sangaré
watchlist.note: A third Brentford asset, and the one with the highest ceiling of the three. The case was always the defensive-contribution rate rather than the fourteen on debut; the new risk is a club that has spent the entire window adding to the same midfield.

week.worked: The best mid-price spine of the five: Ndiaye nine, Szoboszlai eight, Rogers eight, Calafiori nine, João Pedro eleven — forty-five of his fifty-eight from players priced between £5.5m and £7.5m, and no chip spent to get there. Fourth of eleven, second of the five.
week.didnt: Twelve points on the bench, nine of them Gvardiol, who started at left-back for City while Hume and Shaw kept their places in the eleven. It is the largest bench score in the room and it is more than the gap between him and the man leading it.
week.next: Nothing needs buying; the order needs reading. The specific question before Friday is whether a £4.5m Sunderland defender being played as a right winger is a defender at all. Everton is the other thing worth an hour: Moyes named all but two of his opening-day eleven in the cup, won 4-0 at Deepdale, and said again that the squad is short before Tuesday — good for Ndiaye’s minutes, complicated for his shirt if a forward actually arrives.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: The only Arsenal asset he owns is a defender. At £6.5m the midfielder costs the same as E.Le Fée, who produced no shots and no chances created.

watchlist.name: De Cuyper
watchlist.note: Seventeen points at £4.6m, and Brighton go to Stamford Bridge without Mitoma, Minteh, Ferguson and Tzimas and with two more at 75%. The attacking returns were the case for him; the injury list is the part that eats them.

week.worked: Two Arsenal picks nobody else in the room has — Havertz and Mosquera — returned twelve, Tzolis added six, Verbruggen kept a clean sheet at £4.5m and João Pedro brought eleven. Five players costing £31.5m made thirty-five of his forty-eight.
week.didnt: Semenyo, his second most expensive outfielder at £8.5m, returned two from a starting City wide role. Maguire was in the middle of both set plays United conceded at Hull, and Greaves and Groß brought four between them. Forty-eight is last of the five.
week.next: His manager answered the bench question for him this afternoon. Asked about Palestra before the cup tie, Alonso said they need to check a little bit more — a second competitive fixture missed by a £5.5m defender who has not yet played one. Aït-Nouri is the same problem in City colours at 0.8% ownership. Neither has cost him a point; both will, on the first weekend a starter is flagged after the deadline has gone.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: He has a Chelsea defender who has not played and no Chelsea midfielder. Thirteen points and the penalties at £9.5m is where that money belongs.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: The player who kept his own pick out of the City side, for exactly the same money. If a City defensive slot is worth holding, this is the one that starts.

week.worked: Sixty-four points, top of the five and second of eleven, six behind the leader. Rogers, Szoboszlai, Ndiaye, Calafiori and João Pedro made forty-five of it between them — five mid-price players rather than one lucky captain, which is the most repeatable week anybody had.
week.didnt: The Bench Boost, played in the first week of the season, returned six: two apiece from Kinsky, Diop and Groß, nothing from Konsa. His starting eleven scored fifty-eight, which is precisely Mr CR7’s total. The chip is not decoration on the lead — the chip is the lead.
week.next: Two of his fifteen are being decided by other people this week. Cash faces Arsenal at Villa Park for a club that has reached broad agreement to sell Jackson at up to £65m, expects that to trigger Watkins to Al-Hilal, and is asking about centre-backs while Palace try to take another target off them. And Konsa sits on his bench at £4.5m having just cost Arsenal a reported £55m — a slot that is only worth holding if he plays, which is an argument about Saliba’s back rather than about him.

watchlist.name: Ajer
watchlist.note: Eight points at exactly Cash’s price. Brentford have since sold Pinnock to Coventry and agreed a fifth signing of the window, so the straight swap is less straight than it looked on Monday.

watchlist.name: Kayode
watchlist.note: Thirteen points from the other Brentford full-back, and the £40m arriving is a left-back rather than a right one. The cheaper way into the same defence, if the same defence is the idea.

watchlist.name: Woltemade
watchlist.note: Osula is carrying a knock at 50%, and Woltemade started Wednesday’s cup tie. The trigger set two weeks ago was one start; a cup start against a Championship side that subdued him for an hour is not quite it. Spurs away first, then the kindest six-game run on the ticker.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Still the biggest collective miss of the opening weekend and the flag has cleared: thirteen points, Chelsea’s penalties, a goal and an assist, and not one of the five owns him. Ownership 11.7% to 14.3% while the room stood still.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: Eleven points at £6.5m. All five own an Arsenal defender, two of them own Tzolis at the same £6.5m, and nobody owns the Arsenal player who outscored both. This has been written every day since the weekend, which means the page is now the thing repeating itself.

watchlist.name: Barry
watchlist.note: A hat-trick and an assist at Deepdale, after a header against Palace on the opening day, in a side Moyes picked almost at full strength. Cup goals are a team sheet rather than a seat — but the team sheet was the part in doubt, and £5.5m is the price of finding out.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Nine points from City’s left-back. One of the five has him and benched him; another has the wrong City defender at 0.8%. Same club, same price, opposite outcomes.

watchlist.name: Gakpo
watchlist.note: Twelve points at £7.0m and under 6% owned, with two bids for Minteh rejected, Sarr now the target and Barcola still in talks. This is a September buy, not a Friday one.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: Thirteen points, the penalties and the calf flag cleared to fully fit — the best midfield return of the weekend, owned by none of the five and by 14.3% of the game.
verdicts.trigger: Two games spent wide rather than at ten, or the calf returning.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: Eleven points, a rise to £7.6m, the number nine shirt — and with Delap gone to Forest and Jackson at broad agreement with Villa, there is now nobody left to contest the minutes.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box, and 67% ownership becomes the risk rather than the floor.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: Tapped in on debut after a club-record move and got the full ninety, in a Chelsea midfield still missing Caicedo and possibly about to lose Enzo to City.
verdicts.trigger: A week wide or on the bench once Chelsea’s central midfield is whole again.

verdicts.name: Sánchez
verdicts.why: Two errors leading to goals at Fulham, and his manager declined to name a goalkeeper for the cup tie today — "we will decide and give the team tomorrow" — with Penders expected to be given a look.
verdicts.trigger: Chelsea getting through Tuesday without signing a goalkeeper, plus two clean sheets.

verdicts.name: Penders
verdicts.why: A £4.5m goalkeeper at 0.1% ownership whose manager would not rule him in or out of tonight’s cup tie while the incumbent is being asked about weekly.
verdicts.trigger: A league start. A cup appearance behind a shaky first choice is a rehearsal, not a seat.

verdicts.name: Caicedo
verdicts.why: Out of the cup tie, with Alonso saying only that he hopes Caicedo makes the weekend — which is why Chelsea’s central midfield has been makeshift for a fortnight.
verdicts.trigger: Ninety minutes against Brighton. Until then every Chelsea midfielder’s minutes are being set by an absence.

verdicts.name: Martinez
verdicts.why: A £5.0m goalkeeper at 4.1% ownership who has told his club he wants to leave, was left out at Brighton with Bizot picked ahead of him, and whose £30m replacement is already signed — with Chelsea now in talks with his representatives.
verdicts.trigger: The window shutting on Tuesday with him still at Villa and back between the posts.

verdicts.name: Enzo
verdicts.why: City are expected to lodge a formal offer before Tuesday at the £120m Chelsea set, and his manager’s answer on selection was "we expect that he’s involved" — which is a sentence about a squad, not a role.
verdicts.trigger: The deadline passing with him at Chelsea and starting in central midfield.

verdicts.name: Palestra
verdicts.why: Ruled out again today — "we need to check a little bit more with Marco" — a second competitive fixture missed by a £5.5m defender who has not yet played a competitive minute.
verdicts.trigger: One competitive start. Until then this is a slot rather than a player.

verdicts.name: Lacroix
verdicts.why: Six points at £6.0m from a back line that conceded twice, in a team on a seventeen-game run without a Premier League clean sheet — but Brighton arrive missing four forwards and carrying two more at 75%.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet against that Brighton side. If it does not come now, it is not coming.

verdicts.name: Welbeck
verdicts.why: Reported as the second of Alonso’s two strikers, and the reporting firmed up today: Delap to Forest at £50m done, Jackson to Villa at up to £65m broadly agreed.
verdicts.trigger: A start with João Pedro rested, or Chelsea signing a forward before Tuesday, which ends it.

verdicts.name: Gonzalo
verdicts.why: Scored on his Fulham debut, has the penalties, and costs £6.0m at 3.1% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: Anyone starting ahead of him once Fulham’s forwards are all available.

verdicts.name: King
verdicts.why: Nineteen, Fulham’s best player on the night by a distance, the near-post equaliser and a shot from range that nearly made it 3-3, at £5.5m and 0.5% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: Two games without ninety minutes. A teenager’s breakout night is a night.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: Two points, ninety minutes, the penalties and the armband from three of the five — a blank that separated nobody, and City have spent the week selling the forwards behind him rather than buying one.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury, or three straight weeks of City creating through the wide players and past him.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: PFA Player of the Year on Tuesday, and sixteen of United’s twenty-one shots at Hull worth under 0.1 expected goals apiece on Saturday. The award is about last season; the shot map is about this one.
verdicts.trigger: A blank at home to Ipswich with the same shot profile, and £12.0m stops being a price and starts being a hole.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Two points, and the Hull post-mortem points at shot quality rather than at the two set plays — the slower problem, not the quicker one.
verdicts.trigger: United blanking at home to Ipswich, which makes the GW4 sale automatic.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: Thirty-one, started all but one of United’s last forty-four, and still being written about as the position United want to reinforce before Tuesday, with Balde named on the shortlist in the gossip columns rather than by anyone at the club.
verdicts.trigger: A left-back arriving before the deadline, or one week out of the side. Either ends a £4.5m pick whose entire case is that he never misses.

verdicts.name: Lammens
verdicts.why: Cheap is not the same as safe behind a defence that lost at Hull to two headers and is now without De Ligt and Ugarte.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in the next three, or enough save points to make the floor worth it.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: One point, and he is the defender in the middle of the set plays United conceded — though with De Ligt out there is currently nobody to take the shirt.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United’s other centre-backs are fit.

verdicts.name: Baleba
verdicts.why: The signing that completed a £155m midfield rebuild is flagged with an ankle injury and no return date, before playing a league minute.
verdicts.trigger: A return date, then a start. A £5.0m midfielder with neither is a lottery ticket at a bench price.

verdicts.name: Amad
verdicts.why: Flagged at 75%, a report that he could be out for up to six weeks, a club declining to clarify either way, and a price now sliding — £6.0m to £5.9m.
verdicts.trigger: A confirmed return date, or a start. A midfielder whose club will not say what is wrong is unownable.

verdicts.name: Šeško
verdicts.why: Zero pre-season minutes became twenty-three at Hull, and the start still has not come.
verdicts.trigger: A start plus a goal and he re-enters as a watch — not before.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: Nine points, a rise to £5.6m, owned by four of the five and by 41% of the game — still the closest thing to a free lunch on the list.
verdicts.trigger: A recurrence of the knee trouble that has followed him around.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: Eleven points at £6.5m and a week later still nobody in the room owns him, which has stopped being an oversight and become a choice.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season’s injury record, or Arsenal’s returns concentrating in Saka and Gyökeres instead.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: Nine points and Arsenal’s penalties at £9.5m, with barely 10% of the game on him.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or rotation through the Champions League weeks.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Six points at £7.5m and 7.2% ownership, in a forward line that has not yet settled around Gyökeres.
verdicts.trigger: Two weeks as a substitute once Arsenal’s attack is fully fit.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: Six points deputising while both Saliba and Timber are out with no return date — the points are real, the seat is borrowed, and a £55m centre-back has just walked in.
verdicts.trigger: Saliba’s back clearing, or Konsa starting. Either ends this pick.

verdicts.name: Konsa
verdicts.why: A reported £55m signing sitting at £4.5m and 11.2% owned with no Arsenal appearance yet, in a defence currently missing both first-choice centre-backs.
verdicts.trigger: One start. If a £55m defender cannot get in ahead of Mosquera, the price is the only thing recommending him.

verdicts.name: White
verdicts.why: Eleven points, the highest of any Arsenal defender, at £5.5m and 6.2% ownership — and the reason is the same injury list that put Mosquera in the side.
verdicts.trigger: Timber’s groin clearing, which returns him to a rotation option at a starter’s price.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: Six points and a debut that got noticed; a quarter of the game is on him now and the price has not moved.
verdicts.trigger: Saka and Rice fully fit squeezing the minutes.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: Central midfield at Newcastle and on Liverpool’s penalties at £7.0m, but he made zero tackles and won three of ten duels there, and the man brought on to steady it did more in half an hour.
verdicts.trigger: Mac Allister starting in the pivot, or a shift back to right-back. Either halves the appeal.

verdicts.name: Gravenberch
verdicts.why: Lost the ball for both Newcastle goals, and his manager’s public answer was that the problem is not personnel — while the club spent the week bidding for wingers.
verdicts.trigger: Liverpool signing a holding midfielder by Tuesday, or one week out of the two-man pivot.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: Twelve points at £7.0m, and Liverpool have had two bids for Minteh rejected, moved to Sarr and are still talking to PSG about Barcola, wanting two signings before Tuesday.
verdicts.trigger: The window shutting with no wide forward arriving. Then he is a buy rather than a maybe.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: Ninety minutes at left-back at Newcastle in a 2-2, and Liverpool’s remaining window money is earmarked for wide attackers rather than full-backs.
verdicts.trigger: One week on the bench, or Liverpool moving to a back three, and £5.5m stops making sense.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: Started at left-back and returned nine — the City defensive seat that actually exists at £5.5m.
verdicts.trigger: O’Reilly reclaiming the left side once Doku is back on 5 September.

verdicts.name: Aït-Nouri
verdicts.why: A substitute at the Etihad with Gvardiol at left-back, 0.8% owned, and still occupying a bench slot in this league.
verdicts.trigger: One start ahead of Gvardiol. Same price, same club, and only one of them plays.

verdicts.name: Guéhi
verdicts.why: Ten points on his first City start, in a back line reshuffled around an injury rather than by design.
verdicts.trigger: One week out of the XI with City’s other centre-backs fit and £6.0m is wrong.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: Eight points from the bench, with Marmoush loaned to Spurs and City having spent the window buying midfielders rather than forwards — the queue in front of him is shorter than it was on Saturday.
verdicts.trigger: A start. The trigger set three weeks ago has not changed and still has not been met.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: Two points at £8.5m from a starting City wide role. Marmoush leaving makes the minutes safer; it does not make the price right.
verdicts.trigger: Two more blanks with Cherki getting the minutes instead, and this is a sack.

verdicts.name: Marmoush
verdicts.why: A loan to Spurs with an obligation to buy at £60m and a medical due in the coming days, which turns a fourth-choice City forward into a possible starter for a side whose manager says it is not a team yet.
verdicts.trigger: A completed medical and a start. Until both, he is a City player who was an unused substitute.

verdicts.name: Grealish
verdicts.why: City’s £6.5m winger at 0.2% ownership is the subject of a Sunderland loan offer, with Everton also expected to try, and a wage negotiation still to have.
verdicts.trigger: The deadline passing with him at City and in the squad. Nothing before that is ownable.

verdicts.name: M.Sangaré
verdicts.why: Fourteen on debut and a rise to £5.6m, but the case is the defensive-contribution rate rather than the two assists, and Brentford have kept buying midfielders all window.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks over the threshold and he is the cheap midfielder of the season. One is a debut.

verdicts.name: Ajer
verdicts.why: Eight points at £4.5m in a side whose press left Spurs without a shot on target until 3-0 down — and Brentford have just sold Pinnock to Coventry while adding Schuster and, at up to £40m, Diouf.
verdicts.trigger: One rotation, or Schuster starting a league game. A £4.5m centre-back at a club buying defenders is a seat on loan.

verdicts.name: Kayode
verdicts.why: Thirteen points and a rise to £4.6m from Brentford’s right-back, and the £40m arriving plays on the other side.
verdicts.trigger: A week out of the side, or the returns turning out to have been one afternoon of set pieces.

verdicts.name: Schade
verdicts.why: A game-high five second-half shots and a penalty won in a 3-0 — the underlying numbers are ahead of the three points.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks of shot volume without a return and the finishing becomes the story.

verdicts.name: Thiago
verdicts.why: Missed from the spot after converting ten of his previous eleven, blanked in a 3-0 win, and Brentford’s run turns hard from GW5.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties to anyone, and £8.0m is a sack the same day.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Leeds play through him and he started; a one-point opener is a dull floor, which is what he was bought for.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or a striker arriving before the window shuts.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: Nine points on Everton’s penalties at £6.0m in a side that opened with a clean sheet, and he kept his place in a near-full-strength cup eleven.
verdicts.trigger: Everton’s fixtures turning, the penalty duty moving, or a forward arriving before Tuesday.

verdicts.name: Dewsbury-Hall
verdicts.why: Eleven points and the opener in a 2-0, then the pass for the first and the drive that made the second at Deepdale — Everton’s chances are going through him at £6.5m and 4.4% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: A second blank in three with Everton conceding, and he goes back to being a hedge.

verdicts.name: Barry
verdicts.why: A hat-trick and an assist in the cup after a header on the opening day, at £5.5m and 2.6% ownership, with his manager saying publicly he wants more still.
verdicts.trigger: A league goal, or Everton signing the forward Moyes keeps asking for. One of those makes him, one ends him.

verdicts.name: Woltemade
verdicts.why: Started the cup tie with Osula flagged, on penalties at £6.0m and 1.6% owned, in front of the best six-game run on the ticker — though West Brom’s shape subdued him for most of the hour.
verdicts.trigger: A league start at Spurs. That is the team sheet the fixtures have been waiting on for two weeks.

verdicts.name: Osula
verdicts.why: A knock at 50% for a £6.0m forward who was ahead of Woltemade a week ago and was not in the eleven on Wednesday.
verdicts.trigger: A clean bill of health and a league start. Until then the Newcastle striker slot is the other one.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Spurs did not have a shot on target until 3-0 down at Brentford, and their manager said they are not a team yet — while the club kept spending past £312m and gave a debut goal to a £75m winger in the cup.
verdicts.trigger: Reassess at GW7 — window shut, players settled, fixtures softer. Until then this is a bench goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Minus one in a 4-0, and the week since has brought a goalkeeper in talks with Chelsea, a record goalscorer with a Saudi fee agreed, a striker signing at £65m and a centre-back search. Arsenal at Villa Park is next.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three, or the window closing with the dressing room settled.

verdicts.name: Watkins
verdicts.why: Al-Hilal are reported to have agreed around £50m with Villa, and the Jackson deal that triggers his exit is at broad agreement between the clubs.
verdicts.trigger: The deadline passing with him at Villa and in the starting eleven.

verdicts.name: Mateta
verdicts.why: The subject of a Villa offer well below Palace’s valuation, from a manager who says publicly he wants to keep him, at a club now trying to hijack Villa’s move for another target.
verdicts.trigger: Tuesday passing with him at Palace. A £6.5m forward with the penalties and settled minutes is then worth a look.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Sunderland pushed him forward into a right-wing role — good for assists, bad for the clean sheets he was bought for.
verdicts.trigger: A second week out of the back line. A £4.5m defender who does not defend is priced wrong for the position.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Plenty of the ball and Sunderland going through him, but no shots and no chances created at £6.0m — and the club spent Wednesday bidding for two wingers.
verdicts.trigger: A return in the next two, or the money goes to a midfielder who takes shots.

verdicts.name: Emersonn
verdicts.why: Nine points and the best underlying attacking numbers of any Ipswich player at £5.5m — a genuinely cheap forward with a role, away at Old Trafford in GW2.
verdicts.trigger: One start on the bench once Ipswich’s attacking signings settle.

verdicts.name: Igor Jesus
verdicts.why: Forest have completed a club-record £50m striker signing, which is not a fee a club pays for a substitute.
verdicts.trigger: Keeping the shirt for two starts once the new man is registered.

verdicts.name: De Cuyper
verdicts.why: Seventeen points at £4.6m, but Brighton go to Chelsea without Mitoma, Minteh, Ferguson and Tzimas and with Kadıoğlu and Georginio at 75% — the attacking returns were the case and the attack is the injured part.
verdicts.trigger: A second attacking return with that forward line unavailable, and this is a buy rather than an argument.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: A clean sheet in a 4-0 at £4.5m, which is the entire job description of this pick.
verdicts.trigger: Steele getting a cup start that turns into a league one.

signals.text: Villa and Chelsea have reached broad agreement over Nicolas Jackson at £47.5m plus £17.5m in add-ons, and his arrival is expected to trigger Ollie Watkins’ move to Al-Hilal. Watkins leaving would mean five of the starting XI that won the Europa League in May have been sold; Emiliano Martinez is expected to follow, with Chelsea in talks with his camp. Villa have also asked West Ham about Jean-Clair Todibo, and Palace are trying to hijack their move for Ordonez.
signals.action: no Villa asset is startable in GW2 and the cheap defenders are not the safe part — the whole spine is being rebuilt in public while Arsenal come to Villa Park

signals.text: Brentford have a verbal agreement with West Ham to sign left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf for £35m plus £5m, a fifth summer signing after Callum Wilson, Mamadou Sangaré, centre-back Jannik Schuster and Jaidon Anthony. Ethan Pinnock has gone the other way, to Coventry.
signals.action: one of the five owns two Brentford players and another has a third on his watchlist. A club that has bought a centre-back and a left-back and sold a centre-back is not a settled back four — read the Leeds team sheet before extrapolating from the Spurs one

signals.text: The £155m midfield rebuild is largely unavailable. Carlos Baleba, the signing that completed it, is flagged with an ankle injury and no return date; Manuel Ugarte (knee) and Matthijs de Ligt (back) are out with no return date either; Mason Mount and Amad are both at 75%.
signals.source: FPL player file, cross-checked against BBC Sport
signals.action: the case against United was shot quality; the case for them was depth. Neither is true this week, and Ipswich at home is the fixture that was supposed to fix it

signals.text: Brighton travel to Stamford Bridge with Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring) and Stefanos Tzimas (knee) out with no return date, Yankuba Minteh not expected back until 28 November and Evan Ferguson until 10 October, and Ferdi Kadıoğlu and Georginio both flagged at 75%.
signals.action: this is the week to price a Chelsea clean sheet properly, and the week to stop treating a £4.6m Brighton defender as an attacking asset

signals.text: Alonso, asked before the Luton cup tie whether he would be available: "We need to check a little bit more with Marco." He has now missed both of Chelsea’s competitive fixtures this season and has yet to play a competitive minute for the club.
signals.action: a bench slot held by a player with no debut is a slot that pays nothing and costs one the first time a starter is flagged after a deadline

signals.text: Out of the cup tie. Alonso: "Hopefully Moi can make it for the weekend." Chelsea started the league opener with Reece James and Lavia in central midfield in his absence.
signals.action: his return is what makes Chelsea’s midfield normal again — which is bullish for the defence and the reason Rogers’ central role has a shelf life

signals.text: Asked whether Mike Penders would play in the cup tie, Alonso said: "We will decide and give the team tomorrow to the players. I prefer they know first." Penders is expected to be given a chance to stake a claim, with Sánchez in the spotlight again after his mistakes in the 3-2 win at Fulham.
signals.action: a first-choice goalkeeper whose manager will not confirm him for a second-round cup tie is not a floor. Chelsea defenders are still worth owning; the goalkeeper is not

signals.text: City are expected to make an offer before the deadline at the £120m Chelsea set in mid-August. Alonso on selection: "We expect that he’s involved. He’s trained, he’s training really well, he’s a good professional and he will be involved." Chelsea are reported to have lined up Bournemouth’s Alex Scott as a replacement.
signals.source: BBC Sport / The Sun via BBC gossip
signals.action: still a hold at £7.0m and nothing more. A midfielder being selected while his club negotiates a nine-figure sale and shops for his replacement is not a seat you can plan around

signals.text: A hat-trick and an assist in a 4-0 win at Preston, following his header against Palace on the opening day. Moyes named all but two of his opening-day starters. "Thierno worked with somebody back home in the summer who tried to change his mindset a bit... generally he has been much better since he came back, but I would still like more."
signals.action: a £5.5m forward at 2.6% ownership whose manager picked him in a near-first-choice cup eleven and then asked for more. The goals are cup goals; the selection is not

signals.text: Moyes fielded almost his opening-day side in the second round, won 4-0, and maintains Everton are short on numbers and quality before Tuesday. Brennan Johnson made his debut and scored; the club are reported to be lining up a forward from Midtjylland and prepared to sell a defender.
signals.action: good news for Everton’s current minutes and a warning about them at the same time. Two of the five own Ndiaye at £6.0m and one owns Dewsbury-Hall — both are safer than a new forward makes them look, until Tuesday

signals.text: He started the cup tie against West Brom with William Osula flagged at 50% with a knock, and was subdued for much of the first hour by West Brom’s fluid 4-4-2 before Newcastle won 3-1 through Harvey Barnes and Bazoumana Touré.
signals.action: the trigger was one start and this is nearly it. Spurs away is the league team sheet that decides whether the kindest six-game run on the ticker is ownable at £6.0m

signals.text: Behind the best six-game run on the ticker, the defence is the thin part: Dan Burn is out until 14 September with an ankle injury, Tino Livramento (calf) and Joelinton are out with no return date, and the £30m right-back Amar Dedic arrived only last week.
signals.action: buy Newcastle’s fixtures through the forwards, not through the clean sheets. The run is real and the back four is a fortnight old

signals.text: Liverpool had bids of £50m and £60m for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh rejected, switched attention to Crystal Palace’s Ismaila Sarr — who is himself now out with a groin injury and no return date — and are still in talks with Paris St-Germain over Bradley Barcola. The club want two wide attackers before Tuesday.
signals.action: twelve points at 5.6% ownership is the right shape of bet at the wrong moment. Wait for Tuesday night, then buy or forget it

signals.text: The £86m signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi completes a midfield rebuilt twice over in one window — Rodri to Barcelona, Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah, Nico González to Newcastle, against Elliot Anderson and Bouaddi in. Marmoush has gone to Spurs on loan with an obligation, and Sunderland have made a loan offer for Jack Grealish.
signals.action: nobody’s City minutes are safe to project from one team sheet, including the ones that produced the weekend’s cheap defensive haul. The exception is the striker, and everyone already owns him

signals.text: A £75m winger scored on his debut in a comfortable second-round win over Charlton, days after four debutants started a 3-0 defeat at Brentford in which Spurs had no shot on target until 3-0 down. Marmoush’s medical is due, taking the summer past £312m. De Zerbi: "I think we are not a team yet, for a lot of reasons."
signals.action: target Spurs rather than own them until the window shuts and the fixtures soften around GW7. Newcastle visit in GW2 and are the better side to be interested in

doctrine.text: Rank insurance is a real cost — price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template assets are default-own; passing needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice — sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul is a match, not a seat. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week — and then check the table before saying it did not matter. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used; it is also, exactly, the six points between first of the five and second.

Buy the line-up, not the scoreboard. Three of the weekend's best mid-price returns came from players who started on a bench or out of position, and two of the room's bench slots are held by players who have not been in a matchday eleven.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro; none owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.

An open window is a team-sheet risk, not a shopping opportunity. In the week before this deadline a first-choice goalkeeper stopped being selected, a record goalscorer had a fee agreed with Saudi Arabia, a City forward was loaned out and a fifth signing landed at a club two of the five are invested in. Buy after the window shuts, not into it.

A cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture. The goals are worth nothing and the selection is worth everything — which is the only reason a £5.5m forward, a flagged striker’s replacement and a £75m debutant are all worth a sentence this week.

roast.text: Mr CR7 finished second of the five without spending a chip, then left twelve points on his bench — nine of them a City left-back who started at the Etihad. Six of them would have put him top.

plan.outlook: Nothing has moved on the pitch since Monday and nothing will before Friday: Le Professeur 64 and second of eleven, Mr CR7 58, Xabi 50, Sir Fergie 49, The Special One 48, with Gunners.exe out in front on 70. Sixteen points cover the five, which is one bench ordering. Everything that has moved is the market, and the calendar is now against the room — the deadline is Friday evening, the window does not shut until Tuesday, and so every decision this week gets made before the team sheets and before the transfers that will write them. Villa have broad agreement to sell Jackson at up to £65m, expect that to send Watkins to Al-Hilal, are in talks over their goalkeeper leaving and are asking about centre-backs, with Arsenal at Villa Park. Brentford have agreed a fifth signing of the window and sold a centre-back. United’s £155m midfield is mostly in the treatment room. Liverpool have gone from Minteh to Sarr to Barcola without signing anybody. Against all of that, the three buys that stand up are the same three that stood up a week ago — Palmer, Ødegaard, Gvardiol — none of them in a transfer story, and none of them owned by anybody here. The honest read is that the market is doing the talking this week and the room should not be. The three real decisions are unchanged: the United block at Old Trafford in GW4, whether anybody in this room ever buys an Arsenal midfielder, and whether a second chip gets spent in August.

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan). A good week used beats a perfect week hoarded — but a gameweek with fifteen fit players in every squad and no doubles anywhere is neither, and one of the five found that out for six points. The sharper version, four days on: the worst week to spend a chip is a week in which the team sheets are being written by a transfer window. That is this week too.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Le Professeur's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.

Settled Gameweek 1 at fifty points and fifth of eleven. Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. Recommended no transfer before Friday: every obvious buy is either one game old, flagged, or in the middle of a transfer.

No transfer recommended for the third run running, two days before the deadline and six before the window shuts — on the explicit grounds that an open window is a team-sheet risk rather than a shopping opportunity (D9). Downgraded Shaw on the reporting that United expect another left-back before Tuesday. Flipped the Gakpo case: the risk is no longer that Liverpool sell him but that they buy over him, with two bids rejected for one winger and two more targets live. Sacked Villa's goalkeeper as a slot, and Forest's incumbent striker on a £50m arrival. Corrected two errors of our own from Monday: The Special One's dead men were on his bench, not in his eleven, and Le Professeur's six-point Bench Boost is not a footnote to his lead, it is the whole of it.

Deadline eve, and no transfer recommended for the fifth run running — Friday’s deadline falls four days before the window shuts, so nothing bought now is bought with the team sheet known. Upgraded Woltemade on Osula’s knock and a cup start, and opened Barry at £5.5m on a hat-trick graded as a team sheet rather than a scoreline. Held Palestra at sack after Alonso said Chelsea "need to check a little bit more" ahead of a second missed fixture, and added the goalkeeper question alongside it. Cooled De Cuyper on Brighton’s injury list rather than on his seventeen points, and warned on Ajer as Brentford bought a fifth player and sold a centre-back. Sacked Baleba, Osula and Grealish as slots rather than players. Minted D10: a cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture.
